newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks rebound at open after Dow bounce.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks rebound at open after Dow bounce.

text.p: Australian shares opened firmer on Wednesday, the market climbing back above the 2,700 level after Wall Street staged a stunning recovery on Tuesday, bouncing 154 points after falling 192 on Monday.
At 10.15 a.m (0015 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 17.9 points firmer at 2,706.3.
The June share price index was up 19 points at 2,710 and at a 3.7 point premium to the underlying index.
Stocks opened higher across the board with rises from resource issues matching industrials, despite a fall in the price of base and precious metals on Tuesday.

"(Japanese Prime Minister) Hashimoto was taken out of context in the U.S. on Monday but the Dow's big fall that day shows the market was prepared to take profits," said Stuart Smith, senior dealer at Brisbane brokerage Lance Jones.
Smith said the movement of the Dow over the past two days showed that U.S. investors were setting levels to buy and sell rather than running with market direction.
"This is typical of a bull market - it self-generates," Smith said.
Traders said that Australian investors were also proving to be far more cautious.
Australia's robust bank sector was leading the market higher with all the majors and most of the regionals higher.

Newspaper speculation that Westpac Banking Corp's proposed takeover of regional bank, Bank of Melbourne (BML) would be cleared by monopolies watchdog, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission, saw both banks higher.
Westpac was 16 cents firmer at A$7.96 (US$5.97) while BML was nine cents up at A$9.54. Westpac has offered A$9.75 per BML share.
One notable exception was the key resource stock Broken Hill Pty Co, which continued to slip ahead of its annual results, due this Friday.
